title: superset-new-prefetch vs upstream on r7g.large and r7g.xlarge

large.new: io-threads 2: main cpu 0, IO thread + poller cpu 1, NIC queue 0 on cpu 0 and 1 on cpu 1
large.upstream: io-threads 2: main cpu 0, IO thread cpu 1, both NIC queues on cpu 0

xlarge.new: io-threads 4: main cpu 0, IO threads cpu 1-3, poller cpu 3, NIC queue i on cpu i
xlarge.upstream: io-threads 3: main cpu 0, IO threads cpu 1-2, all NIC queues and background on cpu 3

method.hardware: server and replica on two instances of the same size; one c8g.metal-24xl load generator per size; one placement group, 0.13-0.27 ms generator round trip
method.build: GCC 11.5, -O3 -flto, jemalloc, identical flags for both builds; prefetch is the same binary as the c8gn prefetch page
method.layout: each build gets its own best layout from a calibration pass (table below), using every vCPU; irqbalance, RPS and XPS off, THP off
method.client: memtier_benchmark 2.5.2 on one host; 9,600 connections at P1, 2,304 at P16, 960 at P64
method.run: 3 reps per scenario, 10 s window after warm-up, medians of the valid reps; same scenarios as the c8g/c8gn suites at one fixed io-threads value
notes: Each build runs at its own best calibrated layout, so io-threads can differ between builds (r7g.xlarge: prefetch 4, upstream 3). In the calibration upstream at io-threads 3 and 4 were within 1-2%.
verdict: win/regress when the median ratio is beyond 5% and the two builds' rep ranges do not overlap, otherwise tie.
r7g network bandwidth is a burst allowance with a lower baseline; cells marked N hit the allowance and are lower bounds on server capacity.
At pipeline 1 the 0.13-0.27 ms round trip is a large share of request latency, so P1 numbers partly measure the network.
Some 16 KB and 128 KB P1 cells have fewer than 3 valid reps: the load generator did not finish within its time limit.
p100 includes connection setup; use p99.9.
